- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., sentiment > 0.62 → forecast too high).
- Underestimate when sentiment is persistently low (< 0.4) or shows early decline; model fails to adjust downward.
- Lag in correction: model often delays mean reversion, especially after sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral.
- Forecast bias toward higher prices when sentiment is trending upward (e.g., sentiment > 0.75 → forecast 5–10% above true).
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment volatility; model reacts too sharply to single-day sentiment spikes.
- When sentiment is mixed or declining, model tends to underestimate true price movement; apply 2–3% upward bias for such periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates late-period price increases (last 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for final 10 days.
